statement: Audit the pointer table: the first function it exposes, the classes it defines, and the fetch and verify surface it offers.

steps.prompt: Read `ptr_engine/pointer_table.py` and list the top-level functions it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/pointer_table.py` and name the first top-level function it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/pointer_table.py` and report how many top-level classes it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/reference.py` and report how many top-level classes it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/reference.py` and name the first class it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/fetch_tool.py` and report how many top-level functions it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/fetch_tool.py` and name the last top-level function it defines.
Read `ptr_engine/fetch_batch.py` and report how many top-level classes it defines.
Compare the class count you found in `ptr_engine/pointer_table.py` at step 3 with the class count you found in `ptr_engine/reference.py` at step 4 and say which is larger.
Read `ptr_engine/outcomes.py` and report the string value of `OK`.

final_question: Using the function name you identified at step 2 — do not restate it — report how many top-level classes the same file defines.

checkpoints.question: How many top-level classes does `ptr_engine/reference.py` define?
What is the name of the last top-level function in `ptr_engine/fetch_tool.py`?
